featured_videos.title: Carnivores - Give Me 12-Minutes, I'll Give You 6 Reasons to AVOID Salt !!!
featured_videos.creator: Bart Kay - Health Science
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivores - Give Me 12-Minutes, I'll Give You 6 Reasons to AVOID Salt !!!
featured_videos.commentary: Here's the thing. Bart's basically saying what our community already figured out but couldn't quite articulate. That one commenter who went from medicated and numb to salting everything and feeling normal? That's the real story. The salt panic is another case of someone reading one study and treating it like gospel, when your body's actually pretty good at telling you what it needs. Most of us don't need to overthink the shaker. Meat already has sodium, and if you're sweating or feeling off, your body will let you know. This is why carnivore works. it strips away the noise and lets you listen to what's actually happening instead of following a 25-step protocol.

featured_videos.title: Why Fat Loss Stops on Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: Why Fat Loss Stops on Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The dairy thing keeps coming up in these comments, and honestly, it's one of the first things I check with clients hitting a stall. Not because dairy is "bad". it's not. but because it's easy to overeat when everything tastes amazing and doesn't trigger hunger signals the way plant foods do. Some people genuinely do better dropping cheese and cream for a few weeks to reset, like that commenter mentioned. The lifting weights point is solid too. If you're not building muscle while losing fat, your body has less reason to keep dropping the scale. And that quote about gravity? That person got it exactly right. The scale is just one tool, and sometimes the real wins are what you can't measure. how your clothes fit, your energy, your joints moving better. If you've hit that stubborn 10-pound wall, it might not be that carnivore stopped working. It might just be time to get specific about what's actually happening under the surface.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore on a Tight Budget: 10 Cheap Foods That Still Deliver Nutrition
featured_videos.creator: KenDBerryMD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore on a Tight Budget: 10 Cheap Foods That Still Deliver Nutrition
featured_videos.commentary: The community's response says everything. People aren't just grateful for budget tips, they're relieved that someone with credentials is saying out loud what they already know: you don't need to be rich to eat carnivore. The comments keep circling back to one thing, Dr. Berry's lack of pretension. No gatekeeping about grass-finished this or that. Just honest talk about spam, eggs, and ground beef as legitimate nutrition. That's what's resonating here, and honestly, it's the opposite of what wellness culture usually sells us.

featured_videos.title: 25 years Of Carnivore Advice In Just 15 Minutes
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Eric Westman - Adapt Your Life
featured_videos.editorial_title: 25 years Of Carnivore Advice In Just 15 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Westman nails something the internet loves to gloss over: there's no one carnivore script that works for everyone. Look at these comments. you've got strict carnivore folks thriving, people doing KetoVore with a few veggies, others finding that sweeteners wreck their adherence, and someone literally choosing meat because it keeps them out of the hospital after hernia surgery. That's not confusion. That's real life. The "effortless weight loss" myth is exactly what trips people up, and I've seen it happen in my coaching too. You can eat the right foods perfectly and still plateau if you're not tuning into *your* individual response. The sweetener debate in these comments is telling. some people lose control around erythritol, others use monk fruit and do fine. What matters most is paying attention to what actually happens in your body, not what the protocol says should happen.

featured_videos.title: I Have Finally Lost My Mind...August Will Be Tough
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Have Finally Lost My Mind.August Will Be Tough
featured_videos.commentary: This is less about losing his mind and more about recognizing what actually works. The community is clearly onto something with sardines, and the consistency is striking, sardines plus eggs is showing real results for people who've hit plateaus or need a reset. August as a focused month makes sense, it's tactical, not crazy. What's interesting here is the support angle that keeps showing up in the comments, people doing this together with partners or family, which changes everything about whether you stick with it or bail. Worth watching how this plays out because extreme simplicity like this often reveals what your body actually responds to when you strip everything else away.

featured_videos.title: Meat & Fruit - 1 Month Follow Up - What Happened?
featured_videos.creator: pigmie
featured_videos.editorial_title: Meat & Fruit - 1 Month Follow Up - What Happened?
featured_videos.commentary: The comment about "at least two months" really landed, and honestly, that's where most experiments fail. One month with fruit mixed in isn't really testing carnivore or animal-based eating, it's testing snacking habits. The adaptation period is real, your body needs time to shift fuel sources, and you can't tell what's working when you're still halfway in. That said, the commenter who mentioned every diet has people who thrive on it? They're right too. The magic isn't in the diet itself, it's in whether you can actually stick to it and whether your markers improve. Some people do great with fruit and animal foods together, others need strict carnivore to feel the difference. The real test isn't winning a debate online, it's whether you feel better, sleep better, and your bloodwork backs it up.
